newsitem.title: USA: VLSI Technology unveils new chip design.
newsitem.headline: VLSI Technology unveils new chip design.

text.p: VLSI Technology Inc said Monday it unveiled two new custom chip processes that are aimed at its customers in the communications, digital entertainment and high-performance computing markets.
VLSI said it plans in the fourth quarter of 1997 and the first quarter of 1998 to roll out semiconductors composed of lines of circuitry 0.25 and 0.20 micron wide.
The company's stock rose one to 19-1/4 in late morning trading on Nasdaq.
The new processes can integrate up to 72 million logic transistors on a chip, which is about three times more than the current 0.35 micron-wide chip made by the company, VLSI said.
Rich Beyer, VLSI president and chief operating officer, said the new designs will let customers choose operating voltages without compromising performance, power consumption or density.

"The new processes will result in longer battery life, speedier computing performance and smaller footprints for end- products such as cellular phones, television set-top boxes and advanced computers and workstations," he said.
The VLSI VSC9 2.5-V process, or 0.25 micron chip, targets communications and digital entertainment applications featuring mixed analog/digital signal architectures.

The 1.8-V VSC10, or 0.20 micron chip, delivers high performance for high-gate count computing applications at lower power consumption levels than the VSC9 process, the company said. VLSI said its new chip-making process is partly a result of a joint technology collaboration with Hitachi Ltd.
